recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core FHIR follow-up is needed for FHIR-8244 unless a future work group decision explicitly requests a distinct literal QH/qh concept in addition to the existing Q1H every-hour abbreviation.
issue_request: FHIR-8244 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 MnM request to update the Data Types Timing.code value set. The final resolution was to add qh, q4h, q6h, and qod, with comments discussing common medication timing abbreviations such as qd, qh, q4h, q6h, qid, and qod.
initial_application: The Jira application comment cites svn revision 6123. Git commit 6e45ed2fb4d013f7f2498db5672be81c5b632ecc, '#8244 - new codes in Timing.code + generate data elements,' applied the issue to source/datatypes/timing.xml by adding QD, QOD, Q4H, and Q6H rows and updating the Timing.code display. The literal qh/QH row was not added in that hunk, but the current same-value-set history now represents every hour as Q1H through FHIR-13520.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists Timing as a datatype, so source/datatypes/timing.xml and the Timing datatype narrative are current build inputs. Later FHIR-9239 migration work moved the seed-era TimingAbbreviation rows to http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/v3-GTSAbbreviation. FHIR-13520, already represented on the combined branch, added Q1H for every hour and other common timing abbreviations while noting QD and QOD were already supported. FHIR-20609, also already represented, later added C/Continuous to the same value set.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source has QOD, Q4H, and Q6H rows from the seed-era request, the related QD row added with the issue, and Q1H for the every-hour concept now used by the Timing Abbreviations value set. The datatype narrative documents formal meanings for QOD, QD, Q4H, and Q6H.
